paper.title_en: Transient resonances of chaotic orbits in magnetized black hole spacetimes: an event-based frequency-ratio diagnostic
paper.abstract_en: The geodesic equations of the Kerr spacetime are separable, and this separability is what makes orbital dynamics around black holes tractable. An external electromagnetic field removes it, the motion turns chaotic, and the orbit wanders between resonances for irregular and unequal intervals; a long-time Poincaré section returns a single static blur, so that it records where an orbit has been but not when. We introduce the sliding-window frequency ratio, an event-based diagnostic that counts polar turning events within a window of fixed radial-cycle number and returns the local ratio of the two frequencies without any spectral decomposition; for regular motion with bounded count deviations, the error falls off as the window widens. We first establish that a single globally chaotic orbit in a magnetized black hole spacetime pays temporally ordered visits to distinct resonances, and that the corresponding section structure appears only in those intervals that the event counts select. A charged orbit in magnetized Kerr spacetime dwells near 3/5 and later near 4/7, opening fivefold and sevenfold structures, while a photon in Schwarzschild--Melvin spacetime holds 4/5 across a fivefold pattern. Because we keep every event time, we can replot each selected interval as its own section, and integer counts then agree with phase-space geometry. These visits control the phase accumulated along an orbit, and they therefore bear on any orbit-based probe of strong-field black hole geometry.
